Model description

Source: vignettes/model-description.Rmd
model-description.Rmd

This page states the three published models in one notation, every prior with its default, and the argument each symbol is set through. The model pages cite it and repeat none of it. The statements are those of Stone and Gosling (2025), s. 2, with the corrections CRAN AddiVortes made in 0.6.8, and they are the statements the core crate documents in docs/models.md.

The mean function

A tessellation T is a set of b centres c_1, …, c_b in the space of a subset of d of the p covariates. The cell of centre c_l is the set of x nearer to c_l than to any other centre, over those d coordinates, so the cells are a Voronoi partition. A tessellation with cell values M = (mu_1, …, mu_b) is the piecewise-constant function

g(x; T, M) = mu_l   where c_l is the nearest centre to x,

and the mean function is a sum of m of them:

f(x) = g(x; T_1, M_1) + ... + g(x; T_m, M_m).

Each tessellation is a weak learner, held small by its priors, and the sum is flexible; this is the construction of BART (Chipman, George and McCulloch 2010) with a tessellation in place of a tree. A boundary oblique to the axes is one cell boundary here and many splits there.

Distance is Euclidean on covariates scaled to [-0.5, 0.5] over their training range, with two exceptions the covariates page describes: a categorical column takes a mismatch distance, and the columns of a sphere take the great-circle angle.

The priors on a tessellation

For each tessellation j, independently:

  • Cells: b_j - 1 ~ Poisson(lambda_c).
  • Active covariates: d_j - 1 ~ Binomial(p - 1, omega / p), the subset drawn uniformly given its size.
  • Centre coordinates: each coordinate of each centre ~ N(0, sigma_c^2) on the scaled covariates.
  • Cell values: each mu ~ N(0, sigma_mu^2), with sigma_mu = w / (k sqrt(m)) and w a half-width the outcome model owns: 0.5 on the response scaled to [-0.5, 0.5] for the Gaussian model, 3 on the latent scale for the probit model. The sum of m tessellations then has prior standard deviation w / k, so the prior on f(x) puts most of its mass across the range the model works on.

The sampler is the backfitting Gibbs sampler of Algorithm 1 in Stone and Gosling (2025), with the six structural Metropolis-Hastings moves of its Appendix B on the centres and dimensions of each tessellation and a closed-form draw of the cell values.

The three models

Gaussian 

y_i = f(x_i) + e_i,   e_i ~ N(0, sigma^2)

sigma^2 ~ nu lambda / chi^2_nu,   lambda: Pr(sigma < sigma_hat) = q

sigma_hat is the residual standard deviation of a least-squares fit (the sample standard deviation where that fit is degenerate). Nothing is fixed.

Probit 

y_i in {0, 1},   P(y_i = 1 | x_i) = Phi(c + f(x_i))

The latent variance is fixed at 1, since the model does not identify it; the offset c defaults to Phi^-1(ybar). The sampler is the data augmentation of Albert and Chib (1993): a latent z_i ~ N(c + f(x_i), 1), truncated to the side of zero its label demands, is drawn before each sweep, and the ensemble is updated as in the Gaussian model with z - c as the response and unit variance.

Heteroscedastic 

y_i = f(x_i) + s(x_i) e_i,   e_i ~ N(0, 1)

s^2(x) = v(x; T'_1, V_1) * ... * v(x; T'_m', V_m')

with m’ variance tessellations whose cell values are inverse-gamma,

v ~ Inv-Gamma(nu' / 2, nu' lambda' / 2),
lambda' = lambda^(1 / m'),   nu' = 2 / (1 - (1 - 2 / nu)^(1 / m')),

which makes the prior mean of s^2(x) equal to the prior mean of the Gaussian model’s sigma^2 whatever m’ is (Pratola, Chipman, George and McCulloch 2020, s. 3.2); nu > 2 is required. The variance ensemble shares lambda_c, omega and sigma_c with the mean ensemble, and one sweep updates it given the residuals y - f, then the mean ensemble with per-observation precision 1 / s^2(x_i).

Symbols and arguments

Symbol Meaning Argument Default
m mean tessellations term_params(tessellations = ) as mean_params 200
m’ variance tessellations term_params(tessellations = ) as variance_params 0, none
k cell-value prior spread term_params(k = ) 3
lambda_c cell-count prior rate term_params(lambda_c = ) 5
omega prior mean active covariates structure_params(omega = ) min(3, p)
sigma_c centre-coordinate scale geometry_params(sigma_c = ) 0.8
nu noise prior degrees of freedom gaussian_outcome(nu = ) 6
q noise prior calibration quantile gaussian_outcome(q = ) 0.85
c probit offset probit_outcome(offset = ) Phi^-1(ybar)
burn-in, draws, thinning the sweep schedule general_params() 200, 1000, 1

thiessen_control(tessellations = ) is a shortcut for the first row. The default lambda_c of 5 follows CRAN AddiVortes 0.6.8 and later; the paper reports 25, and term_params(lambda_c = 25) is that setting. The control surface page reads every default back from the core.

What a fit returns

Quantity Gaussian Probit Heteroscedastic
predict() posterior mean of f(x) posterior mean of Phi(c + f(x)) posterior mean of f(x)
predict(type = "draws") f(x) per draw Phi(c + f(x)) per draw f(x) per draw
predict(type = "latent") f(x) per draw c + f(x) per draw f(x) per draw
predict(type = "variance") sigma^2 per draw, constant over x not defined s^2(x) per draw
predict(interval = "prediction") from N(f(x), sigma^2) not defined from N(f(x), s^2(x))
sigma() posterior mean of sigma 1 not defined
log_lik() Gaussian Bernoulli Gaussian at s^2(x)
posterior_predict() replicates of y labels replicates of y

The draws of posterior::as_draws_df() carry mu[i], the mean function at each training row; sigma under the Gaussian model; and cell_count and dimension_count, the mean cells and mean active covariates per mean tessellation.
